Deligne-Serre, Formes modulaires de poids 1, Ann. Sci. ENS (4) 7 (1974), Thm 4.1 with (4.1.1), pp. 513-514, as printed: for f != 0 a (cusp) form of type (1, eps) with eps(-1) = -1 that is an eigenvector of the T_p, p not dividing N, with eigenvalues a_p (Tau Ceti EigenformAwayFromLevel N 1, no normalization a_1 = 1), a continuous rho : G_Q -> GL_2(C) with finite image, unramified outside N, with tr rho(Frob_p) = a_p (the T_p-eigenvalue F.eigenvalue p) and det rho(Frob_p) = eps(p). The coefficient form a_p = coeff g p (from a_1 = 1) and eps(-1) = -1 (parity lemma, TauCeti Parity.lean:113) are glue in DSThm966EV.dsThm966_of_printed (coeff-fix).

carirr-refold, consequence of Darmon-Diamond-Taylor 1997 Thm 3.1 (proved: CarayolRefold.frob_of_DDT31 from carirr-odd's transcription CarayolDDT.CarayolDDT31), with the Frobenius clause in the normalization the manuscript reads off Carayol 1986 Theoreme (A) (diophantine_zq.tex L9784-9796): for a printed newform f (Tau Ceti Newform N 2, psi = f.chi) with number field K_f and a place lambda | l, a continuous rho : G_Q -> GL_2(K_{f,lambda}) that is irreducible (Ribet 1977), unramified at p not dividing N l with arithmetic Frobenius of trace a_p and determinant p psi(p) (polynomial X^2 - a_p X + p psi(p)), and with codim V^{I_p} + integral_0^infty codim V^{G_p^u} du = v_p(N) at every p != l (Carayol Thm A + conductor of local Langlands + Casselman 1973 Thm 1; packaged in DDT 3.1). Oddness is proved from the Frobenius determinant (CarayolRefold.odd_of_frobDet, one Chebotarev element). Carayol's own form (sigma_lambda(pi)|G_{Q_p} <-> pi_p under local Langlands) has no Lean form (no pi_{f,p}, Weil-Deligne representations or local Langlands in Lean). Replaces carayolThmAIrr.

r16-thm1b: Shimura 1973 Thm 1 in consequence form (GLUE, pending review), one row. For a newform f in S_2(Gamma_1(N)) with nebentypus chi, the kernel's model X of X_1(N), Jacobian J, Hecke operators T_p = xi_p, : K_f finite over Q, and there is a triple (A, nu, theta) with Shimura's clauses (i) nu surjective with connected kernel, (ii) nu o xi_n = theta(a_n) o nu at n = p and n = p^2 (xi_{p^2} = T_p^2 - p

), (iii) dim A = [K_f : Q], and IsAfQuotient (ker nu = I_f J: nu kills I_f J and is universal for that), unique up to a nu-compatible isomorphism over Q among triples with (i)-(iii). Printed (AI page read): C = Ker(nu) (p. 525), C from the ideal annihilating f intersected with End(J) (p. 526), uniqueness up to isomorphisms over Q (p. 526), dimension and tangent space from m = 1 via q-expansions (p. 527). ON THE SPOT steps: C = I_f J (the ideal is ker rho, saturation, Hecke relations in both directions); (ii) for all n from p and p^2 via xi_{p^2} = T_p^2 - p

(a theorem step, the Hecke relation); nu-compatible isomorphisms. Euler clause and (iv) not in this row.

Grothendieck's semistable reduction theorem as stated in Silverberg-Zarhin, Ann. Inst. Fourier 45 (1995), Theorem 3.4, pp. 405-406 (proof: SGA 7 I, Exp. y3-printed, consequence of Buzzard, Duke Math. J. 87 (1997) Thm 2.1 and Cor. 2.3 at U = V1(5), where M_U d = 30 (author's preprint: Thm 2.1 p. 5, Cor. 2.3 p. 7): a proper smooth curve X over Z[1/30] with a closed immersion into some P^N over Z[1/30], and an FEC (Buzzard's false elliptic curve: an abelian scheme of relative dimension 2 with a ring homomorphism iota : O -> End; injectivity of iota is automatic over a nonempty base, README B-1) over X with a V1(5)-structure (a section Q with 5Q = 0 and iota(3 + 2k)Q = 0, nonzero at every geometric point), universal for such data over every Z[1/30]-scheme S: exactly one g : S -> X over Z[1/30] admits an O-compatible cartesian square carrying Q' to Q, and that square is unique. Unprinted steps: Buzzard's V1(5) for a choice of his fixed kappa with kappa(3 + 2k) = diag(1, 0) mod 5 (README B-5); uniqueness of the square is the absence of automorphisms in the proof of Cor. 2.3 (Lemma 2.2); projective over the affine base gives the closed immersion; no polarization in the data. One of the eight rows that replace y3FullThreeRepZ30 (Y3Buzzard.y3FullThreeRepZ30_of_printed_min5); prints quoted and unprinted steps written out in ZInQKernel/Contrib/OneProof/Y3FullThreeRepZ30/README.md.

On a Z[1/30]-scheme no residue characteristic divides 3. y3-printed, consequence of Buzzard, Duke Math. J. 87 (1997) section 1, the sentence after Def. 1.1 (M prime to d = 6, printed without proof): for an FEC (Buzzard's false elliptic curve: an abelian scheme of relative dimension 2 with a ring homomorphism iota : O -> End; injectivity of iota is automatic over a nonempty base, README B-1) over a Z[1/30]-scheme S there are a closed subscheme Z of A, finite, etale and surjective over S, whose T-points are exactly the generators of full level-5 structures (P with 5P = 0 such that a |-> iota(a)P is a bijection O/5O -> A_t[5] at every geometric point t), and an action rho of G = (O/5O)^x on Z by iota of fixed lifts, with Z x G -> Z x_S Z an isomorphism (the torsor condition, as a kernel-pair square). y3-printed, consequence of Milne, Abelian varieties (1986) Cor. 2.2 (p. 3) and Prop. 17.5(b) (p. 37 of the author's retyped edition) with Buzzard 1997 section 1 (the canonical principal polarization, preprint p. 3): let theta be an automorphism over S of an FEC (Buzzard's false elliptic curve: an abelian scheme of relative dimension 2 with a ring homomorphism iota : O -> End; injectivity of iota is automatic over a nonempty base, README B-1) commuting with iota(O), s : Spec k -> S a geometric point with char k not 2 or 3, and P in A_s(k) such that a |-> iota(a)P is a bijection O/3O -> A_s[3]; if theta fixes P, it fixes every point of A_s(k). Unprinted steps: theta fixes 0 since iota(0) = 0, so it is a homomorphism on the fibre; theta preserves Buzzard's polarization by its uniqueness (README B-2, B-3). Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Forum Math. Pi 1 (2013), Cor. 1.8 with Thms 9.1, 9.3 (diophantine_zq.tex lem:de-rham-descent L10954-10965, step C3) with the Hodge numbers of `H¹_dR(A/F)` (L10996): `H¹_et(A_F̄, ℚ_p)` of an abelian variety of dimension g over a finite `F/ℚ_p` is de Rham with Hodge jumps in [0, 1] and `dim Fil¹ D_dR = [F:ℚ_p] g`, over Mathlib's pro-étale `Scheme.EllAdicCohomology`. **Theorem 5.3 of the 11/5 manuscript (restricted converse, `hyp:RC`), over the genuine Selmer
condition.** For every positive squarefree `ℓ ≡ 11 (mod 12)`,
`corank_{ℤ₂} Sel_{2^∞}(E_ℓ/ℚ) = 1` implies `ord_{s=1} L(E_ℓ, s) = 1`, where
`E_ℓ : y² = x(x - ℓ)(x + 3ℓ)` (`ZInQ.Manuscript.curve`) and `ord_{s=1}` is
`ZInQ.Manuscript.AnalyticRankOne`. It is `ZInQ.Manuscript.RestrictedConverse` at the predicate
`SelmerCorankOne`.

**The Cassels–Tate pairing for the curves `E_ℓ`** (`SelmerTwoPower.CasselsTatePairing` at
`E_ℓ : y² = x(x − ℓ)(x + 3ℓ)` for positive squarefree `ℓ ≡ 11 (mod 12)`, the curves of Theorem 5.3 and
Lemma 5.4).

Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, 2nd ed. (2009), Appendix C,
Evidence 16.5.5, p. 453, rank-one line. The Hasse–Weil L-function is represented
by its analytic continuation from the half-plane of absolute convergence.
Kind: consequence, GLUE. Silverman reports this line; the records derive it from
Miller, LMS J. Comput. Math. 14 (2011), Thm 4.4 (`silvermanRankOne_of_miller`).
